title: Woman trapped, injured in second incident on MBTA Davis escalator this year
author: Darin Zullo
bullets: A woman was injured on an MBTA Davis Station escalator when her clothing got trapped, similar to a previous fatal incident.
A fellow rider hit the emergency stop button to help the injured woman, who sustained a hand injury and was hospitalized.
The MBTA issued safety reminders for escalator use, urging awareness of loose clothing and emergency stop button locations.

title: 2 men arrested after allegedly stealing chain, wallet at knifepoint in Dorchester
author: Darin Zullo
bullets: Two men, Deivi Yoander Sanchez Aguasvivas and Luis Miguel Ramirez-Astacio, charged with armed robbery in Dorchester.
The suspects allegedly robbed a woman at knifepoint, stealing her chain and wallet, before fleeing on a blue moped.
Aguasvivas was arraigned in Roxbury court, while Ramirez-Astacio had a warrant for multiple robbery-related charges.

title: It’s not too late to submit your idea for $2 million in Boston spending
author: Morgan Rousseau
bullets: Boston extends participatory budgeting deadline to August 7, allowing residents to submit project ideas for $2 million funding.
Submissions should propose one-time investments under city authority, focusing on advancing racial and social equality.
Final voting on proposals will occur between January 15 and February 15 after review and community forums.

title: Watch: Ceddanne Rafaela hits home runs in back-to-back at-bats
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Ceddanne Rafaela hit back-to-back home runs in the Red Sox game against the Dodgers on Saturday night.
Rafaela's homers came in the first and third innings, with a 389-foot and a 402-foot shot to left-center field.
Including Friday's game, Rafaela hit three home runs in two days, raising his season total to 14 by the third inning.

title: Red Sox reportedly attempted to acquire shortstop Elly De La Cruz, turned down by Reds
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: Red Sox attempted to trade for Cincinnati Reds shortstop Elly De La Cruz but talks fell through.
Boston's offer for De La Cruz predominantly involved prospects but did not meet Cincinnati's expectations.
The Red Sox continue to seek a shortstop upgrade before the August 3 trade deadline.

title: Drake Maye says his shoulder ‘feels great’ as Patriots training camp continues
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Drake Maye confirms his shoulder 'feels great' after Super Bowl LX injury, looking forward to Patriots training camp.
Patriots upgraded offensive roster by adding A.J. Brown, who is adjusting to New England's playbook and Vrabel's coaching.
Patriots face a challenging 2026-27 schedule, starting with a Super Bowl LX rematch against the Seahawks in Week 1.

title: If July’s stretch of dominance wasn’t enough, the Red Sox’ win Friday proved they’re plenty capable of a postseason run
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: The Boston Red Sox beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 5-4 on Friday, showing postseason potential.
Ceddanne Rafaela led the comeback, while Jarren Duran and Andruw Monasterio contributed key RBIs.
Despite injuries, the Red Sox continue their successful run ahead of the MLB trade deadline.

title: Red Sox fend off Dodgers, 9-4, in grindy series opener
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Red Sox beat Dodgers 9-4 in series opener, highlighted by Ceddanne Rafaela's go-ahead home run.
Boston secured its 21st win in July, marking the franchise's best single-month performance in history.
Reliever Brayan Bello pitched four scoreless innings, maintaining the lead for Boston with a 0.69 relief ERA.

title: Gabe Jacas makes his Patriots debut and other takeaways from Day 7 of training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Gabe Jacas made his Patriots debut on a limited basis after recovering from a knee procedure.
The Patriots' defense recorded two interceptions during unscripted drills in their third padded practice.
Undrafted free agent Tanner Arkin impressed with his blocking skills and earned first-team reps as a tight end.

title: Mass. to be 4th state to roll out EBT chip cards to curb fraud
author: Morgan Rousseau
bullets: Massachusetts to roll out new chip-enabled EBT cards statewide in August to prevent benefit theft, announced Gov. Maura Healey.
Nearly 1 million residents receive SNAP benefits, with cards accepted at 5,500 retailers, based on Gov. Healey's statement.
State collaborated with retailers to update payment terminals; new cards can be locked via DTA app or customer service.
